claims.claim: Global data center electricity consumption was approximately 415 TWh in 2024, representing about 1.5% of global electricity consumption
Global data center electricity consumption is estimated at 448-536 TWh in 2025
claims.notes: Gartner: 448 TWh, Deloitte: 536 TWh (about 2% of global consumption)

claims.claim: Global data center electricity consumption projected to reach 945-1,000 TWh by 2030 (doubling from 2024)
claims.notes: IEA: 945 TWh, Gartner: 980 TWh, Deloitte: ~1,000 TWh base case

claims.claim: Data center electricity consumption has grown at 12% per year over the last five years (2019-2024)

claims.category: AI Share of Data Center Power
claims.claim: AI workloads currently account for 5-15% of data center power use (2024) but could increase to 35-50% by 2030
AI-optimized servers' electricity usage projected to rise from 93 TWh in 2025 to 432 TWh in 2030 (nearly 5x increase)
U.S. data centers consumed 183 TWh of electricity in 2024, more than 4% of total U.S. electricity consumption
U.S. data center electricity consumption projected to reach 426 TWh by 2030 (133% increase from 2024)
China and the US account for nearly 80% of global data center electricity consumption growth to 2030
claims.notes: US: +240 TWh (130% growth), China: +175 TWh (170% growth)

claims.claim: Goldman Sachs projects overall data center power consumption to jump 175% from 2023 levels by 2030
Today's global data center market uses around 55GW of electricity, with AI workloads at 14% of total
Approximately $720 billion will need to be spent on grid upgrades through 2030 to support data center growth
Google's data center electricity usage reached approximately 32 TWh in 2025, up 27% year-over-year and doubled from 2020
Microsoft reported approximately 30 TWh electricity usage in fiscal year 2024, up 27% year-over-year
A ChatGPT query consumes approximately 0.34 watt-hours of electricity (OpenAI official figure)
claims.notes: OpenAI's first official datapoint, not peer reviewed. Independent estimates range from 0.3 Wh to 3+ Wh

claims.claim: AI queries use approximately 10x more energy than traditional Google searches (2.9 Wh vs 0.3 Wh)
NVIDIA H100 GPU consumes approximately 700W per unit, nearly double the A100's 400W
NVIDIA H100 GPUs projected to consume over 13,000 GWh (13.8 TWh) annually, exceeding energy consumption of some countries
claims.notes: Based on projected sales of 3.5 million units at 61% utilization

claims.claim: NVIDIA H100 offers approximately 2x the energy efficiency of A100, with 4x faster training for GPT-3 class models
claims.notes: NVIDIA marketing claim, verified by benchmarks

claims.claim: NVIDIA B200 demonstrates up to 57% faster model training vs H100, with actual power draw around 600W (below 1000W spec)
claims.notes: Early benchmark data from one source

claims.claim: Industry average PUE is approximately 1.56, while top-performing facilities target 1.2 or lower
Google's TTM energy-weighted average PUE is 1.20, using 84% less overhead energy than industry average
Liquid cooling can deliver up to 45% improvement in PUE compared to air cooling, achieving values below 1.2
AI-optimized servers push power densities beyond 50kW per rack, up to 100kW or more, beyond air cooling capability
Natural gas supplies over 40% of U.S. data center electricity, renewables ~24%, nuclear ~20%, coal ~15%
US data center sector contracted 50GW of clean energy by end of Q3 2024 (29GW solar, 13GW wind)
Microsoft signed 20-year PPA with Constellation for 837MW from Three Mile Island; Meta seeking 1.4GW nuclear capacity
PJM Interconnection projects 6GW shortfall in reliability requirements by 2027
claims.notes: Largest US grid operator serving 65 million people

claims.claim: Virginia data centers consumed 26% of state's total electricity in 2023; North Dakota 15%, Nebraska 12%
Global investment in data centers nearly doubled since 2022, reaching half a trillion dollars in 2024
US data center grid-power demand will rise to 61.8 GW in 2025, 75.8 GW in 2026, and 134.4 GW by 2030
Generative AI queries estimated at 15 TWh in 2025, projected to reach 347 TWh by 2030, mostly driven by inference
claims.notes: Schneider Electric report cited by Epoch AI
